title: Gauss's trick for adding 1 to 100
examples: How do you add the numbers 1 to 100 quickly?
What is the formula for 1 + 2 + … + n?

explain.say: The story goes that a teacher in Germany told young Carl Gauss to add every number from 1 to 100, hoping for peace and quiet. Gauss had the answer in moments. Let us find his trick with a smaller sum: 1 to 10. Look at the dots.
Write 1 to 10 forwards, then 10 to 1 underneath. Add each pair: 1 plus 10, 2 plus 9, 3 plus 8. Every pair makes 11! See the rows? There are 10 rows of 11 dots.
10 rows of 11 is 110. But we used every number twice, once forwards and once backwards. So the real sum is half: 55. Can you check it another way?
Pair them up just once: 1 with 10, 2 with 9, up to 5 with 6. That is 5 pairs, each making 11. Look at the dots now: 5 rows of 11, which is 55. Same answer!
Now Gauss's sum: 1 to 100 makes 50 pairs of 101, which is 5050. Brilliant work! The rule is n times n plus 1, over 2. Challenge: what is 1 plus 2 all the way to 1000?

faq.q: How do you add the numbers 1 to 100 quickly?
faq.a: Pair them: 1 with 100, 2 with 99, and so on. Each pair makes 101, and there are 50 pairs, so the sum is 5050.

faq.q: What is the formula for 1 + 2 + … + n?
faq.a: n times n plus 1, divided by 2. For n equals 10 that is 10 times 11 over 2, which is 55.
asks: What is the sum of the first n numbers?

faq.a: He wrote the numbers forwards and backwards and added in pairs. Every pair had the same total, so he only needed one multiplication and a halving.
asks: How did Gauss add up so fast?

faq.q: Why do we halve at the end?
faq.a: Writing the list forwards and backwards uses every number twice. So the total of all the pairs is double the sum you want.

faq.q: What is 1 plus 2 all the way to 1000?
asks: What is the sum of 1 to 1000?

facts: The sum of the whole numbers from 1 to 100 is 5050.

quiz.say: When you pair 1 to 50 as 1 + 50, 2 + 49, …, what does each pair add up to?
quiz.show: When you pair 1 to 50 as 1 + 50, 2 + 49, …, what does each pair add up to?
quiz.why: 1 + 50 = 51, and every pair has the same total.

wrong.1: 49 is one of the numbers, not a pair total.
